comments.body:
Implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 2620
(https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2620). NOT closed, and NO terraform
apply or plan was run — the change lands the IaC and its offline guards only.

## Plan review
PASS, 0 blocking / 2 advisory, signed at head_sha 69cd2b9e15aa6030e5d92c43357b8059a3f5c616
(current origin/main), manifest `rebar-version: 0.13.1 (69cd2b9e15aa)` — i.e. the worktree
build, not a stale global install. `review-plan --status` re-reports `certified`.

Both advisories were honoured in the implementation without touching the description (which
would have invalidated the attestation):
- P6 ac-quality — 3 AC lines bundle deliverables with "and". Noted; each bundled clause has
  its own assertion in the test module, so nothing is unverified.
- G6 — the fourth marker quadrant (declaration absent + proof PRESENT) was unspecified.
  Resolved explicitly as today's behaviour and pinned by
  `test_proof_without_declaration_also_admits`.

## What was config vs. what needed code

`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` did make most of it configuration, as the epic comment predicted:
relocation is a gp3 volume + a UUID fstab mount + `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`/`TMPDIR` on the
review-bot service + a bind mount. Note it takes BOTH env vars — `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` moves
the content-addressed store, but the voter's per-review clone is a plain
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reviewbot-")` and follows `TMPDIR`. That clone is the
one whose bytes scale linearly with concurrency, so setting only the first is half a fix.

What `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` could NOT do is the refusal, and the gap is subtle enough to be
worth recording. S6 already fails closed on an `OSError` from the store root, but an
unmounted volume raises nothing: a mount point whose volume is absent is an ordinary,
writable, EMPTY directory, so `store_root()`'s `mkdir(parents=True)` recreates the store on
root and every gate keeps working — silently — on the disk this epic exists to protect.

Two marker files on two DIFFERENT filesystems make the states decidable:
`/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required` (root, survives an unmount — the declaration) and
`/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted` (the volume, vanishes with it — the
proof). Only declaration-present + proof-absent refuses, raising S6's existing
`GateScratchUnavailableError` BEFORE `_slot_dir()` touches the store. Every other combination
is today's behaviour, so the guard is opt-in by provisioning rather than by rebar version.

Files rather than a knob was deliberate: a `REBAR_*` literal or a `[snapshot]` key would be a
new mechanism, and `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports `active=682 new=0 increased=0`.
The check also runs ahead of the concurrency cap's `0` off-switch and the `fcntl` disarm — a
host that turned the counter off did not thereby consent to losing its scratch volume.

The container binds `/var/lib/rebar` (the mount's PARENT), not the mount point: bind only the
mount point and the container sees an empty directory in both states and the guard can never
fire. A plain host bind, not an `external:` volume, so `config-check.sh` check 5's
compose-up pairing is untouched (`--print-volumes` output unchanged).

## Other notes for S2-S5

- `user_data.sh`'s NVMe-by-volume-id resolution is now ONE function with two callers
  (`resolve_ebs_device` / `mount_ebs_volume`) rather than a second inline copy. The by-id
  symlink fallback exists because the nvme-cli path has been observed to miss; a copy that
  lacked it fails on exactly the boot the fallback was added for.
- `mount -a` does NOT prove a mount happened — a `nofail` entry is skipped quietly — so the
  scratch mount is asserted with `mountpoint -q` and exits non-zero.
- TWO alarms, per the 3e92 precedent: `rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high` (disk_used_percent,
  mount dimension) and `rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted` (a 1/0 heartbeat). A volume that failed
  to mount reads 0% used — perfectly healthy — while every gate refuses, so the first alarm
  structurally cannot answer for the second. Both are `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and
  are now pinned BY NAME in `test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`'s watched set, which is ADR
  0112's standing obligation not to regress bug 3276's missing-data fix by copy-paste.
  Anti-vacuity floors raised 19 -> 21 and 14 -> 16.
- `observability.sh` §2e decides mountedness from the SAME proof marker the refusal reads,
  not from `mountpoint` — a bind mount is a mount point inside a container whether or not the
  host volume is mounted underneath, and monitoring that disagrees with enforcement is worse
  than none. Pinned by `test_the_probe_reads_the_same_marker_the_gate_refusal_reads`.
- Sizing: 50 GiB default, `var.gate_scratch_volume_size_gb`. Basis is the ADR's 3.6 G of
  gate/investigation scratch in the 28 G root working set, against S6's cap of 4 concurrent
  gates; 50 GiB leaves ~42 GiB below the 85% alarm.
- No `prevent_destroy` and no DLM schedule, deliberately: the contents are rebuildable, and
  both runbooks say so, because during an incident that is the difference between clearing
  the volume and treating it as data.

## Verification (all from the worktree venv)

`make lint` exit 0; `make typecheck` "Success: no issues found in 755 source files";
`terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform` clean; `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform
validate` "The configuration is valid" (after `init -backend=false`, which touches no AWS
state). The three gates `make lint` does not cover — `test_mechanism_delta.py`,
`test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`, `test_api_surface_gate.py` — 54 passed, run after
`git add`. Broader sweep of the infra/compose/review-bot-adjacent suites plus all of
`tests/scripts/`: 1590 passed, 23 skipped.

RED-first evidence: the new `tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` was written and run
BEFORE any implementation — 12 failed / 1 passed, and the one that passed
(`test_no_declaration_means_no_assertion`) is the test that asserts today's unchanged
behaviour, so its passing was the correct RED result.

comments.body:
Change 2620 patchset 2 is GREEN on both merge gates: LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1
(https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/33875748018). Not submitted and the ticket is
not closed — left for the caller.

Patchset 2 fixed two real advisories from ps1's review:

1. `observability.sh` §2e published `disk_used_percent` unconditionally. `df` on an unmounted
   mount point answers for the filesystem CONTAINING it, so an unmounted scratch volume would
   have reported ROOT's usage under `mount=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` — a real number about
   the wrong volume, leaving `rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high` reading healthy while scratch was
   gone, or paging "scratch is full" during a root incident. The publish is now gated on the
   mountedness heartbeat; silence is the honest reading and the alarm's
   `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` pages on it. Pinned by a new test.

2. The recovery block in `review-bot-ops.md` recreated only the PROOF marker, which was worse
   than incomplete — `touch <mount>/.gate-scratch-mounted` while the volume is unmounted lands
   the file in the underlying ROOT directory and tells the guard the volume is mounted when it
   is not. That is the silent fallback to root this story removes, performed by its own
   recovery procedure. Recovery now recreates the declaration unconditionally and the proof
   only behind `mountpoint -q`, and explains that the declaration is the marker that is easy
   to lose without noticing (root-resident, so an instance replacement drops it while the
   volume and its proof survive, and the guard is then simply off).

## Follow-up worth a ticket (advisory on ps2, deliberately NOT in scope here)

The refusal guards `gate_admission()`, which wraps plan-review and completion-verifier. The
review-bot's per-review `reviewbot-*` clone (`review_bot/voter.py`) does NOT pass through it,
so on a declared-but-unmounted volume that path still clones — onto root — rather than
refusing. This story's AC3 only required the clone tempdir to RESOLVE to the scratch volume
(it does, via `TMPDIR`), and ADR 0112 puts the refusal at gate admission, so this is a real
gap in the ADR's coverage rather than a defect in the change. It also interacts with ADR 0069:
the code-review path must treat this as a retryable deferral, never an `LLM-Review -1`, which
is exactly the carve-out S6 had to make for congestion. Worth a sibling ticket under the epic.

Two other ps1 advisories were answered rather than changed, with reasoning recorded on the
Gerrit change: the container's write access to the declaration marker (the stack's existing
root-container posture, not something this bind creates, and belongs with container hardening)
and the text assertion pinning observability and the refusal to ONE notion of "mounted"
(a same-source constraint that behaviour cannot observe; `mountpoint` and the proof marker can
legitimately disagree inside a container, and monitoring that disagrees with enforcement reads
healthy while every gate refuses).

S1 MERGED as Gerrit change 2620 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1). No Terraform was applied -- only fmt, and validate after init -backend=false (local provider resolution, no AWS calls, no state access).

THE EPIC'S PREDICTION HELD, WITH ONE CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR did make relocation
configuration-only -- but it takes TWO env vars, not one. REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR moves the
content-addressed store, while the voter's per-review clone is a plain
tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='reviewbot-') and follows TMPDIR. That clone is the path whose
bytes scale LINEARLY WITH CONCURRENCY, so setting only the first is half a fix. Code changes came to
~25 lines; everything else was Terraform and config.

THE REFUSAL IS SUBTLER THAN THE ADR ASSUMED, and this is the part to preserve against a future
simplifying edit: an unmounted volume raises NOTHING. A mount point whose volume is absent is an
ordinary, writable, EMPTY directory -- so store_root()'s mkdir(parents=True) silently recreates the
store on root and every gate keeps working on the disk this epic exists to protect. S6's fail-closed
on OSError cannot see it, because there is no error.

Solution: two markers on two DIFFERENT filesystems -- /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required on root
(survives an unmount) and .gate-scratch-mounted on the volume (vanishes with it). ONLY
declaration-present + proof-absent refuses, raising S6's existing GateScratchUnavailableError before
_slot_dir() touches the store. Files rather than a config knob, so the mechanism ratchet stays at
new=0.

TWO ALARMS, NOT ONE, per the 3e92 precedent: a volume that failed to mount reads 0% used -- perfectly
healthy -- while every gate refuses. The disk-high alarm STRUCTURALLY CANNOT answer for the unmounted
case. Both are treat_missing_data=breaching and pinned by name in the existing
test_alarm_actions_terraform.py watched set (extended, floors raised 19->21 and 14->16), which is ADR
0112's standing obligation not to regress bug 3276 by copy-paste. observability.sh decides
mountedness from the SAME proof marker the refusal reads, so monitoring and enforcement cannot
disagree.

PATCHSET 2 FIXED A HAZARD PATCHSET 1 CREATED, and it is worth recording because it is a perfect
inversion: the ps1 recovery runbook said 'touch <mount>/.gate-scratch-mounted' -- which, while the
volume is unmounted, lands the file on ROOT and tells the guard the volume is mounted when it is not.
THE RECOVERY PROCEDURE FOR THE SILENT FALLBACK WOULD HAVE PERFORMED THE SILENT FALLBACK. Now the
declaration is recreated unconditionally and the proof only behind 'mountpoint -q'. Also fixed: df on
an unmounted mount point answers for the CONTAINING filesystem, so the ungated metric would have
published ROOT's usage under mount=<scratch>.

RED-first: 12 failed / 1 passed before implementation, and the one that passed asserts today's
unchanged behaviour -- the correct RED result rather than a broken oracle.

ARCHITECTURAL GAP FILED, not absorbed: 1ef8-c849-5801-4eee (fillable-starry-aruanas, p1). The refusal
guards gate_admission(), which wraps plan-review and completion-verifier -- but the review-bot's
clone path does not pass through it, so on a declared-but-unmounted volume that path still clones
onto root. AC3 only required the tempdir to RESOLVE to the volume (it does) and ADR 0112 puts the
refusal at gate admission, so this is a gap in the architecture rather than a defect here. It needs
ADR 0069's retryable-deferral treatment so a refusal never becomes an LLM-Review -1.

compiled_state.description:
# S1 — Isolate review-gate scratch on a dedicated EBS volume

## Why
Gate snapshots (`rebar-gate-snapshots`) and the review-bot's per-review `reviewbot-*` clones
share the OS/root filesystem, so a review burst can wedge the whole Gerrit host (bug
`3276-2f81-8c75-4ddd`, 5h outage). ADR 0112 decision 3 moves that workload onto its own EBS
volume, mirroring the existing `/var/gerrit` split from ADR 0012.

## Design — mostly config + Terraform; ONE narrow code guard

`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` already parameterises the snapshot store's base dir
(`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:peek_store_root`), and `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` honours
`TMPDIR`, so RELOCATION needs no code: it is a Terraform volume + a host mount + two compose
env vars + a bind mount. New code is needed for exactly one thing — the ADR consequence that
an unreachable scratch volume must REFUSE, not silently fall back to root.

**Terraform** — `aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch` (gp3, `var.gate_scratch_volume_size_gb`,
**no** `prevent_destroy`: scratch is rebuildable, unlike the data volume),
`aws_volume_attachment.gate_scratch` at `/dev/sdg`, two new `user_data` template vars
(`gate_scratch_volume_id`, `gate_scratch_mount`), an output, and two CloudWatch alarms.

**Host** — `user_data.sh` resolves the NVMe device by volume id with the SAME loop the data
volume uses (extracted into a shell function so there is one copy, not two), formats
idempotently, mounts by UUID via `/etc/fstab`, then asserts `mountpoint -q` and `exit 1` if
the mount did not take. It writes the two marker files below.

**Container** — `docker-compose.yml` review-bot gains `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` and `TMPDIR` set to
the scratch path and a host bind of the mount's PARENT (`/var/lib/rebar`), so both markers are
visible inside the container. A plain bind, not an `external:` volume, so `config-check.sh`
check 5's compose-up pairing is untouched. `compose-up.sh` pre-creates the parent dir.

**The refusal (AC3's teeth).** A bare mount point is an ordinary directory: if the volume is
not mounted, `store_root()`'s `mkdir(parents=True)` silently recreates the store on ROOT — the
exact regression the ADR forbids. Two marker files make the two states distinguishable without
a new mechanism (no new env var, no new config key, so the mechanism ratchet stays at `new=0`):

- `<mount>/../.gate-scratch-required` — the DECLARATION. Lives on the root filesystem, so it
  survives an unmount.
- `<mount>/.gate-scratch-mounted` — the PROOF. Lives on the VOLUME, so it disappears with it.

`gate_admission()` checks this BEFORE `_slot_dir()` (which would otherwise mkdir on root) using
the side-effect-free `peek_store_root()`; declaration present + proof absent raises S6's
existing `GateScratchUnavailableError`, which already routes as a retryable non-verdict. Both
markers absent = no dedicated volume declared = today's behaviour, so no laptop, CI runner, or
existing operator is affected.

**Observability** — `observability.sh` §2e publishes `disk_used_percent` for the scratch mount
(`InstanceId` + `mount` dimensions, following §2) and a `gate_scratch_mounted` 1/0 heartbeat
(dimensionless, following §2b). Two alarms in `monitoring_autodeploy.tf` beside the root alarm,
both `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` with the 300/3/2 window and both SNS actions, so bug
`3276`'s missing-data fix is carried, not copy-pasted.

**Sizing.** Default 50 GiB, matching the data volume: the ADR measured gate/investigation
scratch at 3.6 G on root, and S6 bounds concurrent gates at 4, so 50 GiB leaves ~42 GiB below
the 85% alarm — an order of magnitude of headroom over observed peak. It is a variable, per
ADR 0112 decision 6.

## Scope
IN: Terraform volume/attachment/variables/output, user-data mount, compose env + bind,
compose-up dir, scratch metric + two alarms, the admission refusal, runbooks, tests.
OUT: Docker/journald/`/var/tmp`/container-layer caps (S2–S5); no `terraform apply` — this
change is written and validated only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Terraform declares a gate-scratch EBS volume, attachment, size variable, tags and an
      output; the volume carries NO `prevent_destroy` and its comment states it is rebuildable
      scratch rather than source-of-truth data.
- [x] `user_data.sh` resolves the scratch device by volume id, formats idempotently, mounts by
      UUID through `/etc/fstab`, and exits non-zero when the mount point is not a mount.
- [x] The review-bot's snapshot store AND its `reviewbot-*` clone tempdirs resolve to the
      scratch mount (`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` + `TMPDIR` in compose), not to root.
- [x] With the scratch volume declared but not mounted, `gate_admission` raises
      `GateScratchUnavailableError` instead of materialising a store on the root filesystem;
      with neither marker present, behaviour is unchanged.
- [x] The scratch mount publishes `disk_used_percent` and a `gate_scratch_mounted` heartbeat,
      each with its own CloudWatch alarm wired to `aws_sns_topic.alerts` and
      `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.
- [x] `review-bot-ops.md` and `provision-restore.md` document the steady-state location, the
      two alarms, the refusal behaviour, recovery, and the rebuildable-data posture.
- [x] `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports `new=0`: the refusal introduces no new env
      var, config key, or feature flag.
- [x] Portability: every control is Terraform + a Linux mount + env config, proved by local
      pytest and `terraform fmt/validate`; nothing requires a specific CI provider.

## Testing
Each command is run from the worktree with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"`.

- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` — new RED-first tests: the
  declared-but-unmounted refusal, the no-markers no-op, the mounted happy path, the compose
  env/bind wiring, and the Terraform volume/attachment/output/user-data shape.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` — extended (not duplicated) with the
  two new alarms in its `watched` set and raised anti-vacuity floors.
- `pytest -q tests/scripts/test_observability_disk_pressure.py` — the scratch metric and the
  mounted heartbeat are published by the real `observability.sh`.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py` — S6's admission suite still passes.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py
  tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` — the three gates `make lint` does not cover.
- `make lint && make typecheck`
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform && terraform -chdir=infra/terraform validate`

No `terraform apply`, and no `terraform plan` against live state: this story lands the IaC and
its offline guards only.

Resolve, format and mount the scratch volume by UUID; fail loud if it is not a mount; write the declaration and proof markers.
Add the scratch disk-used and mounted-heartbeat CloudWatch alarms beside the root-disk alarm.
Set review-bot REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR and TMPDIR to the scratch path and bind the scratch mount's parent into the container.
Pre-create the scratch parent host directory so the bind mount resolves.
Publish the scratch mount disk_used_percent and the gate_scratch_mounted heartbeat.
Refuse admission when the scratch volume is declared but not mounted, before any store mkdir touches the root filesystem.
Document the scratch location, the two alarms, the refusal, and recovery.
Document scratch volume provisioning and its rebuildable-data posture.
New test module: the unmounted-volume refusal, the no-marker no-op, compose wiring, and the Terraform/user-data shape.
Extend the existing alarm guard with the two new alarms and raised anti-vacuity floors.
Extend S6's admission suite if the new pre-check changes its fixtures.
Assert the scratch metric and mounted heartbeat are published by the real observability.sh.
